title: Microrecipes: token evolution and compact examples for tables/charts/buttons
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Purpose:
Create a compact, example-first documentation page (a ‘microrecipes’ format) that explains token evolution strategies and provides small, copy-paste examples for buttons, tables, and charts.

Scope:
- A single doc page per component family (Buttons, Tables, Charts) plus a short tokens primer.
- Each doc contains: 3 short usage recipes (do/don't style), a migration snippet mapping old token names to new ones, accessibility notes, and Storybook links with live examples.
- Keep samples minimal and focused on common edge-cases we see in production: dense-data tables, interactive sort/filter controls, and chart color shifts for theming.

Goals:
1) Reduce ambiguity for engineers migrating token names or replacing hardcoded values.
2) Surface practical anti-patterns we repeatedly see (e.g., mixing semantic tokens with component-specific overrides).
3) Provide ready-to-use Storybook stories and short CSS/JSON snippets so adoption friction is low.

Deliverables:
- 1 markdown-like doc per family (Buttons/Tables/Charts) stored in docs repo with compact snippets.
- Storybook stories flagged as "microrecipe" for each snippet.
- Migration mapping file (CSV/JSON) in repo and a shrink-wrapped checklist for migrations.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Three microrecipes published each for Buttons, Tables, Charts (usage, migration, do/don't)
A2: Migration mapping included and verified against current tokens in tokens-v2.json
A3: Storybook contains matching live examples and is accessible via the doc page links
A4: Design review approved (UX + Accessibility) and PM sign-off on rollout messaging
A5: Devs can follow the checklist and migrate a simple table in under 30 minutes
comments: 2025-02-19 Maya Chen: Kickoff — drafted outline and example list. Prioritized Tables because of frequency of bugs in dense views.

2025-02-25 Sofia Ruiz (Accessibility): Quick pass — contrast ok for primary/secondary tokens but flagged chart palette for colorblind friendliness; added recommendations to recipes.
2025-02-27 PM Review (Liam O'Connell): Suggested adding migration checklist and a rollback pattern (feature flag + A/B) for Dedicated customers.
2025-03-01 Engineering feedback (Rina Das): Request to include small JS snippet showing recommended KV-cache-safe rendering for table row virtualization (pointer to runtime advice).
2025-03-04 Arjun Patel: Added migration CSV and linked PR. Ready for design review on 2025-03-06. GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/842

notes: Implementation notes: keep examples < 20 lines where possible; prefer JSON token examples over long CSS blocks to reduce cognitive load.
We will tag Storybook stories with metadata: {category: 'microrecipe', difficulty: 'easy'} — stored as story meta, not user-facing.
For Tables: include recipe around 'column density' showing when to collapse columns vs horizontal scroll.
For Charts: include color token swap example for 'brand-accent' -> 'semantic-success' when data state changes.
For Buttons: recommend token-fallback order: component-size -> component-state -> semantic-purpose; discourage inline color overrides.
